research.niche: Compressor dehumidifiers and home-humidity products (dehumidifiers 10-20 L/day, hygrometers, moisture absorbers) for damp coastal and new-build flats
research.summary: Not recommended. Damp flats are a real problem in Albania, but the earlier scan was wrong to call this market thin. Neptun alone lists 10 compressor dehumidifiers (Beko, Ariston, De'Longhi, Rowenta, Philips) from 12,999 ALL (EUR 145). Megatek lists about 13 (Haier, Argo, Irradio, Ariston, Niklas, Alpina), Shpresa sells a Xiaomi 13 L for 17,990 ALL, and Gjirafa50 and Supermart also stock them, so a 16 L unit already sells for about EUR 190-200 with instalment plans. Duty is not the problem: dehumidifiers fall under HS 8479.89, which is 0% MFN in Albania, so Chinese-made units pay no duty. The problem is the numbers. A small buyer lands a 16 L unit at about EUR 125-142, and after courier, ads, COD refusals and a warranty reserve, the planned first order loses about EUR 170 even if everything sells. The stress test comes out at about -EUR 570, and the best all-B2B case is still about -EUR 175 to -250. It clearly loses to the host-kit benchmark (stress test about +EUR 100, advisor average 54), and the most useful part of it is a small add-on to the host kit rather than a business of its own: an auto-restart dehumidifier plus hygrometer for property managers' empty winter flats, bought only against paid orders.

regulation: Customs: dehumidifiers with a built-in compressor are normally classed under HS 8479.89 (EU BTI practice 8479 89 97). Albania's MFN rate is 0% on all 4 national lines (WITS 2022), so no proof of origin is needed. Confirm the classification with a broker, because 8415.82 would mean 10% duty.
Import VAT 20% (recoverable once VAT-registered), scanning fee EUR 22 above EUR 1,000 declared, broker about EUR 80-150 per shipment. Every sale needs a real-time fiscal invoice.

Electrical safety: the unit must carry CE marking under LVD/EMC/RoHS, plus RED for WiFi models, with EU Declaration of Conformity and Albanian-language labels and instructions on every unit. Grey-imported EU stock usually has the paperwork, but Chinese-direct OEM units need the documents checked.

Consumer law: 14-day withdrawal for distance sales and 2-year seller liability. A failed compressor in month 18 is the seller's problem, so you need a repair partner or spare units. Grey-imported De'Longhi units may not be covered by the brand's local service network.

Refrigerant: modern units use R290 (propane, about 40-100 g). Shipping falls under UN3358 with special provision 291, which secondary sources say exempts machines holding less than 12 kg of flammable gas. Couriers and freight forwarders may still ask for a declaration. Older R134a units are F-gas products.
WEEE / end-of-life take-back obligations for electrical equipment importers in Albania were not verified.
No product licence is needed for dehumidifiers or hygrometers. Anti-mould sprays and fungicides are biocides and should be avoided (registration needed).

first_order.description: One groupage pallet from Germany or Italy: 10 Comfee/Midea-class 16 L R290 dehumidifiers (buy about EUR 115 ex-VAT, estimate), 4 De'Longhi DEX212SF 12 L (about EUR 165, estimate) and 40 digital hygrometers (about EUR 4.50). Sales split 50% B2C (Instagram/Facebook with COD) and 50% B2B to hosts and property managers at a 10% discount, delivered phone-confirmed. Not recommended; shown to quantify the loss.
first_order.calc_notes: Python, standard margin model. Goods EUR 1,990 + pallet freight EUR 350 + broker EUR 100 + scanning EUR 22 = EUR 2,462 ex-VAT. Import VAT about EUR 468 paid up front and recovered later, so cash needed is about EUR 2,930. Duty 0% (HS 8479.89, WITS 2022). Landed per unit: 16 L EUR 142.3, DEX212SF EUR 204.1, hygrometer EUR 5.6. Prices incl. 20% VAT: 16 L EUR 189 (16,970 ALL, matching Beko BDP016 16,999 and Haier 16,999-17,999), giving EUR 157.5 net; DEX212SF EUR 279 (25,049 ALL, against Neptun 29,999), giving EUR 232.5 net. Per dehumidifier sale: courier+COD EUR 11 (13 kg), ads EUR 14 per B2C sale, warranty reserve 5% of net (compressor appliance), B2B price -10% with 7% refusals, B2C refusals 13% each costing two-way delivery. Contribution at 100% sold: 16 L -EUR 206 (10 units), DEX212SF -EUR 59 (4), hygrometers +EUR 97; total -EUR 168 on EUR 2,710 net sales (-6.2%). Stress test, 70% sold: 15% refusals give contribution -EUR 120, then minus EUR 450 running costs = -EUR 570; 12% refusals give -EUR 566. Unsold stock worth about EUR 739 at landed cost is left over. Best case: 14 units at EUR 100 (BigBuy tier), EUR 250 Italy pallet, all B2B self-delivered at EUR 189 gives +EUR 20 per unit, +EUR 281 if all sell, stress -EUR 253; at EUR 199 the stress test is -EUR 176. B2C at EUR 189 loses about EUR 5 per unit even at a EUR 100 buy price. Buying direct from China (30 units, LCL) lands at about EUR 99 each, but MOQ and compliance rule it out for a beginner.

risks: Local shelf prices are at or below EU retail: Neptun's Beko 10 L is EUR 145 and its 16 L units are EUR 189-200, all with 24-month instalments. A small importer cannot undercut these chains.
Negative contribution after courier (13 kg parcels), ads, COD refusals and warranty reserve. The B2C channel loses money on every unit at competitive prices.
Two-year seller liability on a compressor appliance, with no brand service network for grey imports. One failure can wipe out the margin on 5-10 units.
Strongly seasonal (Oct-Mar). Stock bought late arrives after the peak, and unsold bulky units tie up cash for 9 months.
Bulky goods: a 0.08-0.1 m3 carton, about 13 kg, raises freight share, courier cost and storage needs for someone with a day job.
Classification risk: if customs choose 8415.82 instead of 8479.89, duty goes from 0% to 10%.
Power outages (about 40 a year): units without auto-restart will draw complaints, so the spec must include auto-restart and continuous drain for empty flats.
Passive absorbers and hygrometers are cheap commodities sold by Gjirafa50 and Temu (under the EUR 22 de minimis), so there is no margin in them on their own.

research.niche: Home backup power: portable LiFePO4 power stations (0.3-2 kWh) and folding solar panels for Albania
research.summary: The need is real. Albania has about 40 outages a year, the June 2024 regional blackout hit it, Tirana neighbourhoods keep reporting cuts, and many homes have water pumps that stop when the power goes. But this is a poor first business for a part-time beginner. Each unit costs EUR 185-420 to buy, so EUR 1,500-2,500 covers only 4-6 units, and the fixed costs land on very few items: dangerous-goods pallet freight of EUR 250-450, a broker, and 10% duty on HS 8507.60. Brands sell direct in the EU at heavy discounts (1 kWh units at EUR 474-599), which leaves almost no room for a small dealer. Contribution margin is about 10-18% even at 1.5-1.6x the EU price, and the stress test comes out at about -EUR 890, or about -EUR 270 if unsold stock is counted at cost. Gjirafa50 and Foleja already sell EcoFlow, Anker SOLIX and other brands at high prices, so the gap is narrow. It loses clearly to the host-kit benchmark (average score about 3.3/10 against 54/100; stress -EUR 890 against +EUR 100). At most, revisit it as a pre-sold, deposit-backed B2B add-on (cafes, rental hosts, home offices) once a dealer account and 0%-duty classification are confirmed.
demand_evidence: Albania has about 40 power outages a year, the worst in Europe (albania-market-context skill, Nov 2026). With power at about EUR 0.09/kWh there is no savings story; demand rests on reliability alone.

'power station' is dominated by 'battersea power station', meaning almost no buying intent.
Retailers see some demand: Gjirafa50 and Foleja list several EcoFlow, Anker SOLIX, Platinet, Dedra and Sandberg power stations (see local_sellers).

Self-producers of electricity are growing: 3,137 in total with 284 MWp installed (https://scantv.al/english/lajme/shqiperia/rriten-veteprodhuesit-e-energjise-elektrike-numri-total-arrin-ne-i27585), a sign of interest in solar and storage.

Tirana water is on only about 5 h/day in some areas, and homes and rentals depend on electric pumps and tanks. An outage stops the water too, which is the strongest pitch to rental hosts (skill facts; no direct survey found).
EcoFlow's EU web store does not ship to Albania (its 24-country list excludes it: https://eu.ecoflow.com/pages/shipping-policy), so Albanians cannot buy cheaply from the brand direct.

regulation: Customs: HS 8507.60 (lithium-ion accumulators) carries 10% Albanian MFN duty (WITS 2022). Folding panels HS 8541.43 are 0%. A power station could arguably be classed 8504.40 (static converters, 0%), so ask Albanian customs (DPD) or the broker for a binding tariff ruling before the first import. All main brands are made in China, so EU/CEFTA/Turkish preferences do not apply even when buying from an EU distributor.

Import VAT of 20% plus scanning fee (EUR 22 over EUR 1,000 declared) plus broker (EUR 100-150, likely higher for dangerous goods). VAT registration from the first import; real-time fiscal invoice on every sale; 0% profit tax up to ALL 14m.

Dangerous goods: power stations over 100 Wh are fully regulated Class 9 (UN3480, or UN3481 if packed with equipment). Road groupage needs ADR documents and packaging, and the Italy-Durrës ferry leg falls under IMDG. Ask the forwarder (e.g., Dyrrahsped) for DG acceptance and surcharge. Domestic couriers (Posta Shqiptare, ADE, Ultra) must also accept 10-14 kg lithium parcels for COD (unverified).

Product conformity: CE-type conformity (low voltage, EMC, battery safety tests such as UN38.3) and declarations of conformity from the supplier. Albania has transposed EU New Approach rules, and the importer is responsible for documentation.
Albanian-language labels and manual or safety leaflet on every unit (importer name and address, ratings, safety warnings).

Consumer law: 14-day withdrawal for online/COD sales and 2-year seller liability. The brands have no service centre in Albania, so warranty failures mean shipping a dangerous-goods item back to the EU at the seller's cost.

Waste/extended producer responsibility: Law 74/2025 on extended producer responsibility (https://leap.unep.org/en/countries/al/national-legislation/law-no-742025-extended-responsibilities-producing-entities) applies to importers. Battery and electronics fees or registration under its implementing decisions may apply (details unverified).
Marketing: do not claim savings (power is cheap) or that a unit can run a whole home. Advertise real run-times only.

first_order.calc_notes: Python, standard margin model, EUR 1 = 89.78 ALL. Buy prices ex-VAT are estimates (no dealer price list obtained): 1 kWh EUR 420, panel EUR 220. Freight EUR 300 (Italy groupage EUR 150-300 + DG surcharge) split by weight. Duty 10% on (goods + freight) for stations, 0% for panels. Broker EUR 120 + scanning EUR 22 spread over 4 units. Landed cost: 1 kWh EUR 587.5, panel EUR 310. Net price ex-VAT: 1 kWh EUR 741.6, panel EUR 305.4. Per order: courier+COD EUR 12/10; refusals cost 2x courier; ad EUR 5 per sale (warm B2B); warranty reserve 5%. Unit contribution: 1 kWh EUR 98 (13.2%), panel -EUR 36 (-11.9%). Cash = landed EUR 2,073 + import VAT outlay EUR 386 (recoverable) = EUR 2,459. Profit if all sold EUR 258 (10.2% of net sales of EUR 2,530), before running costs. Stress test (70% sold, EUR 450 running costs, unsold stock at zero): -EUR 891 at 7%, -EUR 895 at 12%, -EUR 897 at 15% refusals; -EUR 273 if the unsold 30% is counted as stock at cost. Scenario A (B2C mix, 6 units, ads EUR 8-25/sale): cash EUR 2,652, profit all sold EUR 327 (11.4%), stress -EUR 890/-893 (12%/15% refusals), -EUR 220 with stock at cost. If customs accepted HS 8504.40 (0% duty), Scenario A improves to EUR 468 all sold and -EUR 749 stress. Scenario C (5 no-brand Alibaba 1 kWh at EUR 275 + EUR 450 DG freight, sold at 59,900 ALL): profit all sold EUR 314, stress -EUR 874. Main drivers: few high-value units carry high fixed and dangerous-goods freight costs, and EU street prices (EUR 474-599 for 1 kWh) cap the Albanian price. Suggested Albanian prices are already 1.5-1.6x EU street.

risks: Thin margins: EU brands sell direct at 40-50% off list all the time (1 kWh at EUR 474-599), so dealer margin is small and Albanian buyers can compare prices online or have diaspora relatives bring units in.
Dangerous-goods logistics: lithium units over 100 Wh need ADR/IMDG paperwork. Forwarders and couriers may refuse them or add surcharges, and returns or warranty shipments are costly.
No local service centre: a 2-year seller liability on a EUR 900 battery product with no brand repair network in Albania means one failed unit can erase the margin of the whole order.
HS classification risk: 10% duty (8507.60) versus 0% (8504.40) decides whether the numbers are only negative or very negative; it needs a binding ruling.
Dealer access unconfirmed: EcoFlow, Bluetti, Jackery and Anker may refuse a one-person Albanian start-up or impose MOQs; the EcoFlow EU store does not ship to Albania.

Demand is mostly for short outages (minutes to a few hours). Cheap substitutes such as router UPS units, Temu power banks under the EUR 22 duty-free limit, and fuel generators ('gjenerator ne shitje' is the top Google query) cover much of the need.
Competition: Gjirafa50 and Foleja already list EcoFlow, Anker SOLIX, Platinet, Dedra, Sandberg and ProXtend, with fast shipping and their own marketing.
Product cycles are fast: new models and price cuts every few months can leave a small stock overpriced or outdated.
COD on high-ticket items: a refused EUR 890 parcel ties up cash and adds two-way heavy courier cost; deposits are essential.
Seasonal and news-driven demand: spikes after blackouts or storms. Do not size stock on spikes.

research.niche: Electric-car charging gear (Type 2 to GB/T adapters, portable mode-2 chargers, Type 2 cables, wallboxes with an electrician partner)
research.summary:
This niche does not beat the host-kit benchmark. It roughly matches it on the CFO stress test (+EUR 112 against about +EUR 100) but loses on complexity, safety liability and competition. My beginner scores add up to 29/60.

Demand is real and growing fast. About 4,100 pure EVs were first-registered in January to April 2026 (13.5% of all registrations, 2,830 of them BYD), many are grey imports from China, and diesel costs over ALL 200 per litre. The earlier claim that "nobody sells chargers" is wrong. Gjirafa50.al lists a Defenzo Type 2 cable at ALL 11,350, and its Kosovo site lists wallboxes and mobile chargers. AnGroup, Panele Besi, Konekta and more than 20 MerrJep listings sell wallboxes from ALL 23,000, Type 2 to GB/T adapters at ALL 13,300 and portable chargers. Many of these are cheap Chinese units.

Duty is 0% on every relevant HS line (8504.40, 8544.42, 8536.69, 8537.10; WITS 2022), so EU or EFTA origin gives no advantage and Chinese sourcing is fine. That also means anyone can import cheaply. Only light, compatibility-driven items make money. GB/T adapters show about 39% margin and portable Type 2 chargers about 17%. Cables, GB/T portable chargers and stocked wallboxes come out near zero or negative after air freight. A small first order of 15 adapters and 10 portable chargers (about EUR 1,976 cash including recoverable import VAT) shows about EUR 353 profit after running costs if all sell, and +EUR 63 to +EUR 112 at 70% sold.

Best use: a side line sold B2B to Chinese-EV import car lots and electricians, alongside the host kits, rather than a replacement.

regulation: Duty: 0% Albanian MFN on 8504.40, 8544.42, 8536.69, 8536.90 and 8537.10 (WITS 2022, all national lines min = max = 0). Origin proof is not needed, and Chinese goods are fine. You still pay 20% import VAT (recoverable; register for VAT from the first import), the scanning fee (EUR 22 if more than EUR 1,000 is declared, otherwise EUR 5) and a broker (about EUR 80-150).

Electrical safety: insist on a CE Declaration of Conformity (LVD and EMC) and test reports: IEC 62196 for connectors, IEC 62752 (in-cable protection device) for mode-2 portable chargers, and IEC 61851 for wallboxes. Keep the technical file; Albania follows EU-aligned conformity rules (exact Albanian transposition unverified).
Albanian-language label and manual on every unit (safety warnings: earthing, no extension leads, use only on a dedicated circuit).
Consumer law: 14-day withdrawal for online sales, 2-year seller liability. Electronics returns and compatibility disputes are likely, so keep a 4% reserve.

Wallbox installation must be done by a qualified or licensed electrician. The household connection may need a check or upgrade (single to three phase, contracted power) with OSHEE. The procedure and any permit are unverified. Apartment buildings may need the administrator's consent for shared parking.
Every sale needs a real-time fiscal invoice (fiscal software about ALL 7,000-19,000 per year). Profit tax is 0% up to ALL 14m until 2029.
No lithium batteries in these products, so no dangerous-goods shipping. Product-liability insurance is recommended because of fire risk.

python3 model, EUR 1 = ALL 89.78. Goods: 15 x EUR 30 + 10 x EUR 85 = EUR 1,300 (estimated from Alibaba listings at USD 27-33 and USD 75-125). Weight 35 kg x EUR 7/kg air express (estimate) = EUR 245. Duty 0. Broker EUR 100 + scanning EUR 22 = EUR 122. Import VAT 20% on goods plus freight = EUR 309 (cash out now, recovered later). Cash needed EUR 1,976 (samples, about EUR 100, sit in the EUR 450 running budget).

Per unit (net of 20% output VAT): adapter net EUR 91.9, landed EUR 39.1, contribution EUR 35.8 (39%); portable charger net EUR 156.9, landed EUR 108.1, contribution EUR 26.7 (17%). This is after courier + COD at EUR 6/8 per order, refusals (B2C 13.5%, B2B 7%, each costing a two-way delivery), EUR 12 ads per B2C sale and a 4% warranty reserve.

All sold: net sales EUR 2,947, contribution EUR 803 (27.3%), minus EUR 450 running costs = +EUR 353.

Stress test (70% sold): contribution EUR 562 - 450 = +EUR 112. The unsold 30% stays in stock at cost (about EUR 500). With 15% B2C refusals and only 30% B2B: +EUR 63. If the unsold stock is written off entirely: -EUR 388.

Dropped lines: Type 2 cable -4% (air freight on a 2.4 kg item, local Defenzo at ALL 11,350); GB/T portable charger 2% (AnGroup at ALL 12,000); stocked wallbox 6% (local sellers at ALL 23,000-24,000).

risks: Fire and electrical-safety liability. Cheap mode-2 chargers and adapters can overheat; a single incident with a customer's car or flat is far worse than a bad towel. Buy only certified units, test samples, and consider insurance.

Compatibility returns. GB/T variants, 1-phase versus 3-phase, car-specific charging limits and CC/CP signalling differences cause 'it doesn't work with my car' returns and support calls, which is heavy for a part-timer with a day job.

Competition is already there and cheap. AnGroup, Panele Besi, Konekta, Gjirafa50 and many MerrJep sellers price Chinese wallboxes at ALL 20,900-24,000 and adapters at about ALL 13,300. Customers can also buy a GB/T adapter on AliExpress for about EUR 40-70 plus VAT, and EU retail is EUR 72-82, so the price ceiling is low.
Zero duty cuts both ways: no origin advantage for EU brands, and anyone (car importers, electricians) can import the same goods directly.
Many new cars come with a charging cable, and car lots may bundle adapters themselves. B2B buyers could become competitors after one order.
Small absolute market: about 1,000-1,250 EVs per month nationally, and only part of them are GB/T grey imports or need a portable charger.
Air freight dominates the landed cost of heavy items such as cables and wallboxes; sea groupage needs volume a beginner does not have.
OSHEE public charging rollout and any household-tariff scheme could change what owners buy: it helps adapters, but may reduce demand for portable chargers.
Frequent power outages (about 40 a year) and voltage problems may be blamed on the charger, causing warranty claims.

research.niche: Premium car care and detailing products (Koch-Chemie, Sonax, Gyeon, Meguiar's, Polish and Turkish brands; snow foam, sealants, microfibre, foam lances; 5 L canisters for detailers)
research.summary: Car culture in Albania is real: an estimated 5,000-7,000 car washes (lavazh), 1.07m vehicles and a small number of detailing studios in Tirana. But the premium segment is already covered. Global Resource Trading (GRT) is Koch-Chemie's official Albanian distributor and also runs Ceramic Pro Albania. Top Auto Parts has a Sonax distribution agreement. ADBL and K2 sell on GjirafaMall, Turtle Wax on Tronix and Supermart, Meguiar's comes in through a Kosovo representative, and Instagram shops such as @albaniadetailingofficial (5.7k followers) resell Koch, Rupes and 3M. Lavazh owners compete on price (a wash costs 600-1,000 ALL) and buy cheap bulk shampoo (20 kg for 4,499 ALL), so the B2B channel the brief hoped for barely exists for a newcomer. Duty is not the problem: polishes are 0%, cleaners 2-6%, EU and Turkish origin 0%. The problems are heavy, low-value liquids, Albanian CLP labels and safety data sheets, and ADR rules for flammable or corrosive products. The best first order I could model (48 own-brand kits plus 10 B2B canisters, about EUR 2,540) makes only about +EUR 260 if everything sells (around 10% margin) and about -EUR 1,010 in the standard stress test. That is clearly worse than the host-kit benchmark (about +EUR 100 under stress, average score 54), and it also ranks below the Petkit backup. Verdict: LOSES to the benchmark. Not recommended for this buyer.

regulation: Law No. 27/2016 'On the management of chemicals' (modelled on REACH and CLP) makes the importer the party placing the product on the market. That brings duties to classify the product, label it, provide a safety data sheet (SDS) and possibly enter it in the national chemicals register. https://leap.unep.org/en/countries/al/national-legislation/law-no-272016-management-chemicals

DCM No. 488 of 29.6.2016 on classification, labelling and packaging is fully aligned with EU CLP Regulation 1272/2008. Hazardous mixtures (most wheel cleaners, alkaline all-purpose cleaners, many sealants and polishes) need Albanian-language CLP labels with pictograms, signal words and H/P statements, plus an SDS in Albanian. https://www.informea.org/en/legislation/regulation-no-488-date-2962016-classification-labelling-and-packaging-chemicals
DCM No. 665/2016 covers import and export of hazardous chemicals (Rotterdam Convention). Normal car care products are probably outside it, but each product's SDS should be checked.

ADR (Albania a party since 2005): flammable sealants, solvent-based products, aerosols and corrosive wheel or alkaline cleaners ship as dangerous goods. Groupage carriers may refuse them or add surcharges. Local couriers may refuse aerosols.

General consumer rules: Albanian label on every unit, 14-day withdrawal right (refusing returns of opened chemicals needs clear terms), 2-year seller liability, a real-time fiscal invoice for every sale, and VAT registration from the first import.

Duty: polishes 3405.30 0%, microfibre 6307.10 0%, foam lances 8424.x 0%, cleaners 3402.90 2% and 3402.50 6% (WITS MFN). EU or Turkish origin with an invoice declaration or EUR.1 gives 0%. Korean (Gyeon) and Chinese goods pay MFN, which is low anyway.

Fixed costs EUR 242: broker 100 + scanning fee 22 + Albanian SDS/label translation and setup 120; origin declaration free, duty 0% (EU origin). Unit labels EUR 0.90 per kit. Launch and samples EUR 100. Landed cost: kit EUR 43.66, canister EUR 34.32. Kit net price EUR 65.83 ex VAT. Kit variable cost EUR 15.47 per sale (courier+COD 6, ads 6, 3% returns reserve, 13% COD refusal x EUR 10 two-way), so contribution is EUR 6.71 (10.2%). risks: The official distributors (GRT for Koch-Chemie and Ceramic Pro, Top Auto Parts for Sonax) plus Instagram resellers already serve studios and enthusiasts. A newcomer has no price edge on the same brands.

Lavazh B2B buyers are price-driven (20 kg shampoo for 4,499 ALL, about EUR 50) and pay cash. Premium 5 L canisters will sell only to a handful of detailing studios, many of which are already tied to GRT.
Liquids are heavy and low in value per kg. Freight plus fixed import costs add about 25% to the goods value on a small order.
ADR and dangerous-goods limits remove the most profitable items (sealants, coatings, wheel cleaners) from cheap groupage and from couriers, especially aerosols.
CLP compliance: Albanian labels and SDS for every SKU, and the possible chemicals-register duty, are paperwork and liability a part-timer can underestimate.
Temu and AliExpress sell foam lances, mitts and microfibre duty-free under EUR 22, which undercuts the accessory part of any kit.
COD refusals on EUR 70-80 kits and the 14-day withdrawal right for opened chemicals.
Seasonality: washing peaks in dusty summer months and falls in winter rain, so an off-season plan is needed.
Brand exclusivity: Polish brands (ADBL, K2) already have regional channels and may refuse a second Albanian reseller.

regulation: Albania-Turkey FTA (in force 1 May 2008): Turkish-origin industrial goods enter at 0% with proof of origin (EUR.1 or invoice declaration; confirm which with the broker). https://dogana.gov.al/english/dokument/2126/fta-with-turkey

Without proof of origin, or if the item is not really made in Turkey (some Turkish brands source from China), MFN applies (WITS 2022): 15% on stainless kitchenware (732393/732394), 10% on glassware (7013), 10% on carpets and bath rugs (5702/5705), 15% on porcelain and ceramics (6911/6912), 6% on plastic housewares (392490). Aluminium cookware (761510) and terry towels (630260) are 0% anyway.

Food-contact materials: Instruction No. 15/2012 under Food Law 9863 and Guideline No. 12/2017 on plastics (partly aligned with EU 10/2011). Get a supplier declaration of compliance and migration test reports for coated pans and glass; AKU can inspect. Act 17/2023 (declaration plus 10% lab tests) applies only to polyamide and melamine kitchenware from China/HK. https://www.ecolex.org/details/legislation/instruction-no15-of-2012-on-materials-and-articles-that-may-come-in-contact-with-food-lex-faoc144200/
Labels in Albanian on every unit (material, importer, care, induction and dishwasher suitability, food-contact symbol).

Standard importer duties: 20% import VAT (recoverable once VAT-registered), scanning fee (EUR 22 above EUR 1,000 declared), broker about EUR 100, real-time fiscal invoice on every sale, 14-day withdrawal right and 2-year seller liability (non-stick coatings that peel are a typical claim).
Non-stick and 'PFOA-free' or 'granite' claims need supplier evidence; do not copy claims without documents.

Buy cost includes 2-3% breakage. Goods EUR 1,370; freight EUR 300 per pallet, allocated by weight; fixed costs EUR 242 (broker 100 + scanning 22 + EUR.1/chamber 40 + Albanian labels 30 + document translation 50) spread over 30 kits; packaging EUR 2.5 per kit. Duty 0% (Turkish origin). Landed cost: basic kit EUR 56.3, premium kit EUR 89.6. Per order, B2C: courier + COD EUR 10-11; ads EUR 8-10; 13.5% refusals, each costing a two-way courier trip; 3% returns and warranty reserve. B2B: delivery EUR 3, 7% refusals. Contribution per kit: basic 21.6 B2C (21%) / 24.4 B2B (28%); premium 47.1 (28%) / 43.9 (31%). All 30 sold: net sales EUR 3,424, contribution EUR 915 (26.7%), EUR 465 after the EUR 450 six-month running costs. Stress test (70% sold, EUR 450 running costs, 13.5% B2C refusals): contribution EUR 640, minus 450 = +EUR 190; unsold stock (EUR 606 landed) kept as inventory. If unsold stock is written off, the result is -EUR 416. Pessimistic case (buy prices about 20% higher, ads EUR 15-18 per B2C sale): margin 15%, stress test -EUR 89. With only 20% B2B the stress test is +EUR 185. Selling the same goods singly fails: a Pasabahce set alone is -82% B2C, a granite set alone 7-9%, a bath-mat set alone -4%.

Single items make no money: low-value glass and bath-mat sets cannot carry a courier fee, COD refusals and ads. Only bundled kits or B2B orders work.
Glass breakage in groupage freight and courier delivery; Polat Cam excludes glass from its damage guarantee.
Origin trap: some Karaca, Emsan and Korkmaz SKUs are made in China. Without a valid EUR.1 or a non-Turkish product, duty is 15% on steel and 10% on glass, which wipes out about half the contribution.
Bulky, heavy goods (5-10 kg per kit) raise courier and storage costs and need space at home.
Buy prices are estimates. Korkmaz may refuse to sell outside its Albanian distributor or ask distributor-level volumes.
Demand tracks construction and rental furnishing cycles; permits fell about 13% in 2025, and summer-home furnishing is seasonal.
Turkish lira swings change buy prices and competitors' prices quickly.
Warranty claims on non-stick coatings within the 2-year seller liability.

research.niche: Water filtration with installation (under-sink reverse osmosis, whole-house sediment filters, cartridge-replacement plan) in Tirana/Durres
research.summary: The water problem is real. Tirana gets water only 5 h/day in some areas, a doctor quoted by ACQJ calls the tap water unsafe, and households already pay about 36,400 ALL/yr for bottled water. Duty is no barrier either: Albanian MFN duty is 0% on HS 842121 and 842199, so Chinese, Turkish and EU goods all enter duty-free. But the beginner's planned model is already being run by several established installers, often at lower prices. Ecosoft Albania/Teoren rents an installed 6-stage RO system with filter changes for 1,390 ALL/month (13,900 ALL/yr prepaid) and offers a 30-day free trial. Albafilters offers RO maintenance from 12,000 ALL/yr with a 10-year warranty, and Albuji and Aquafilter Albania offer free installation. On paper the first order works. 12 installed RO units, 8 whole-house filters and spare cartridges cost about EUR 2,300 cash, and the model gives about +EUR 2,050 if everything sells and +EUR 409 in the stress test. With more realistic plumber fees (EUR 40) and ad costs (EUR 35 per sale) the stress test falls to about -EUR 228. A beginner with a day job also carries plumbing labour, leak liability and an unknown brand against trusted incumbents. Verdict: this niche LOSES to the host-kit benchmark (average 54). It scores about the same as the Petkit backup at best. It works better as an add-on to the host kit (RO taps or jug filters for short-term-rental flats, cafes and offices) than as a standalone business.

regulation: Customs: HS 8421.21 (water filtering machinery) and 8421.99 (cartridges/parts) are 0% MFN in Albania (WITS 2022), so no EUR.1/origin proof is needed for duty. Import VAT is 20% (recoverable), plus a scanning fee (EUR 22 if over EUR 1,000 declared) and a broker (~EUR 100).

No specific licence was found for selling or installing household point-of-use drinking-water filters. Albania's standards body DPS has adopted the EN standards for drinking-water treatment devices inside buildings (membrane devices, softeners, active-media filters, UV), but certification is voluntary. Get the supplier's test reports and materials-in-contact-with-drinking-water declarations (NSF/ANSI 58, WRAS, CE).
Pump/UV models are electrical products: CE (LVD/EMC) documents, plus an Albanian-language label and manual on every unit.
Do not make health claims ('removes bacteria/viruses/heavy metals') without test evidence: consumer protection rules on misleading advertising.

Consumer law: 14-day withdrawal for distance/off-premises sales (get a signed consent before installing) and 2-year seller liability. Leaks under the sink can damage the flat and the neighbours below, so consider liability insurance and use a competent plumber.

Business: QKB registration with trade + installation activity, VAT registration from the first import, and a real-time fiscal invoice for every sale and every monthly or yearly subscription payment. Running costs are about EUR 450 per 6 months.
Courier COD for cartridge parcels; installs are booked appointments (take a deposit to cut no-shows).

first_order.description: One mixed Turkey groupage shipment (or Aquafilter Poland): 12 under-sink 6-stage RO units with mineralizer (4 of them booster-pump versions), 30 annual 10in cartridge sets (sold to these customers and to existing RO owners of other brands), 8 whole-house 20in Big Blue sediment housings, 10 sediment cartridge 2-packs, plus EUR 80 of fittings and tools. Installs by a partner plumber at about EUR 25 each. Prices: RO installed 24,000 ALL, cartridge set 6,500 ALL (below Ecosoft's 9,000), whole-house filter installed 12,000 ALL, cartridge 2-pack 3,500 ALL.
first_order.calc_notes: Python, standard margin model, EUR1 = 89.78 ALL, 20% output VAT. Goods EUR 1,560 (12x70 + 30x12 + 8x25 + 10x8 + 80 fittings). Fixed costs: Turkey groupage 250 + broker 100 + scanning fee 22 = 372. Duty 0%. Landed EUR 1,932, plus recoverable import VAT EUR 362, gives EUR 2,294 cash. Net ex-VAT prices: RO 222.8 / cartridge set 60.3 / whole-house 111.4 / 2-pack 32.5. Per-sale costs: RO plumber 25 + fittings 5 + travel 3 + ad 20, failed visit EUR 15 at a 12% no-show rate; whole-house plumber 20 + 8 + ad 12; parcels courier/COD 5.5 + ad 6 (sets) or 3 (2-packs), refusals 13.5% each costing a two-way delivery of 9.2. Warranty reserve 4% of net sales. Margin per unit after landed cost: RO 32%, sets 50%, whole-house 30%, 2-packs 35%. All sold: net sales EUR 5,699, profit EUR 2,055 (36%), or EUR 1,605 after EUR 450 running costs. STRESS (70% of every line sold, EUR 450 running costs, refusals included, unsold stock written off): +EUR 409. PESSIMISTIC (RO price 22,000 ALL, plumber EUR 40, ad EUR 35 per RO sale; whole-house 11,000 ALL, plumber EUR 30, ad EUR 20; set ad EUR 10): all sold EUR 1,146 (21%), stress test -EUR 228. Labour: about 2 h per install, so about 40 h of plumbing visits in total. Subscription income (cartridges at month 6-12) mostly falls outside the 6-month window.

risks: Entrenched installers already run the exact model: Ecosoft/Teoren rents RO with filter service at 1,390 ALL/month with a 30-day free trial; Albafilters offers a 10-year warranty and free water analysis. A beginner's unknown brand has no price or trust advantage.
Over 3 years our offer (24,000 ALL + 6,500 ALL/yr) costs about 37,500 ALL, against about 41,700 ALL for Ecosoft's subscription. That saving is too small to win customers away from a known brand.
Installation labour and scheduling clash with a day job; you depend on one plumber (need a backup); about 2 h per install.
Leak/water-damage liability in apartments; 2-year seller liability on installed equipment; warranty call-outs eat into margin.
Low pressure and intermittent supply in Tirana: many flats need booster-pump RO or roof-tank set-ups; wrong sizing means complaints.
Low online search volume (Google Trends near 0), so leads come through word of mouth or paid ads with uncertain cost per sale; installs are high-consideration purchases.
Cartridge recurring revenue only starts after 6-12 months and needs a reminder/CRM system; customers may switch to cheap Temu cartridges (under EUR 22, duty-free parcels).
Quality risk on Chinese/Turkish OEM membranes and fittings; inspect samples, keep the local backup supplier (Ecosoft Albania spare cartridges).
The EIB-funded network upgrade could improve Tirana supply over time and weaken the shortage argument (the water-quality argument would remain).
