ranking.niche: Turkish-made home goods sold as 'new apartment' kitchen kits (granite or stainless cookware plus Pasabahce glasses)
ranking.verdict: This is the best of the six, but as a second product line inside the host-kit business, not as a business of its own. It sells to the same property managers and hosts, can come on the same Turkish groupage pallet with the same EUR.1 at 0% duty, and needs no licence. As a separate B2C business it is weaker than host kits. Loose items lose money, glass breaks, and Arteg/Blunavi, Big Market, Eng Home, JYSK and Temu already cover the category.
key_reasons: Same buyers and same Turkish freight route as host kits. Putting both on one pallet splits the broker, scanning and EUR.1 costs between them, which improves the host-kit numbers too.
Little regulation: a supplier food-contact declaration and Albanian labels. No dangerous goods, no installation, no electrical warranty.
It is cheap to stop. Unsold cookware and glasses resell on Merrjep or to hosts at about cost, and they do not go out of date.
It only works as a kit. A Pasabahce set sold on its own is -82% and a granite set on its own is 7-9%. A beginner who drifts into selling single items loses money.
Origin trap: a Korkmaz or Karaca item made in China pays 15% on steel and 10% on glass, which removes about half the contribution.
The +EUR 190 stress result assumes unsold stock is kept and buy prices are guessed. With stock written off it is -EUR 416, and in the pessimistic case -EUR 89.
must_check_before_buying: Get written quotes from Polat Cam or Marmara Zuccaciye (or a trade price from Arteg locally) for the exact granite set, the stainless set and the Pasabahce 6-glass sets, with carton sizes.
Confirm 'Made in Turkey' on every item and that the supplier will issue an EUR.1 or invoice declaration. Ask the Albanian broker which document the Albania-Turkey FTA needs for 7013 and 7323.
Pre-sell at least 10 kits with deposits to the same hosts and managers who buy host kits, and count them separately so the same buyer's demand is not counted twice.
Get the supplier's food-contact declaration of compliance for coated pans and glass, and ask a broker or AKU what is checked at import.
Get a packaging plan for glass (double box) and who pays for breakage, since Polat Cam excludes glass from its damage guarantee.

ranking.niche: Water filtration with installation (under-sink RO, whole-house sediment filters, cartridge plan)
ranking.verdict: The model has the best paper numbers of the six, but for a part-timer it is an installation and service business. It brings plumber scheduling, leak liability in flats above neighbours, and a 2-year seller liability, all against an incumbent I checked. Ecosoft Albania charges 1,390 ALL/month with free transport, free installation, filter changes included and a 30-day no-obligation trial. An unknown beginner brand has no price or trust edge, and the stress result depends on cartridge sales that are unlikely in the first 6 months.
key_reasons: Real, structural need (5 h/day supply in parts of Tirana, distrust of tap water) and 0% duty on 8421.21/8421.99.

The incumbent offer is confirmed on ecosoftalbania.com: 1,390 ALL/month, free install, filter maintenance, 30-day trial, cash after installation. This offer is the hardest kind for a newcomer to beat.
About 40 hours of install visits on weekday daytime appointments conflicts with a day job, and everything depends on one plumber.
A leak that damages a neighbour's ceiling could cost more than the whole year's profit. Liability insurance availability was not checked.
Roughly a third of the stress result comes from selling 21 of 30 cartridge sets to other brands' RO owners. Ecosoft subscribers already get filters included, so those buyers are doubtful.
It fits the host-kit buyers only as a later add-on (RO tap for rental flats and cafes), not as a first business.
must_check_before_buying: Run a no-stock test first: offer 'filtered water for your rental' to 10 known hosts and managers and take deposits before ordering anything.
Line up a plumber, a backup plumber, a fixed fee per install, and a written split of who pays for a leak.
Get a quote for liability insurance covering under-sink installs.
Ask a lawyer or QKB whether installation activity needs a licence or a registered plumbing activity code.
Get supplier quotes and samples (Aquafilter Europe, Aquamab, AFG) and check whether Aquafilter Albania holds exclusivity.
Model it without third-party cartridge sales. If the stress test goes negative, do not launch.

ranking.niche: Electric-car charging gear (Type 2 to GB/T adapters, portable mode-2 chargers)
ranking.verdict: Low capital, light parcels, 0% duty, a growing BYD and Chinese grey-import fleet, and a positive stress result (+EUR 112 with stock kept). For a beginner, though, the risk is lopsided. The first order is unvetted Alibaba electrical gear that charges a customer's EUR 30,000 car at 32A in their flat. 'It does not work with my car' returns and technical support do not fit a day job. AnGroup, Konekta, Gjirafa50 and Merrjep already sell the same goods. It could be a narrow B2B side line through car-import lots later, but not a starting point.
key_reasons: Demand is real: about 4,100 pure EVs first-registered in Jan-Apr 2026, 2,830 of them BYD.

The local price ceiling is confirmed. AnGroup lists the EMA Type 2 to GB/T 1-phase 32A adapter at 13,300 ALL, a portable GB/T charger at 12,000-18,000 ALL and wallboxes at 52,000 ALL. A 9,900 ALL adapter has some room, but EU retail is EUR 68-82 and AliExpress is lower.
Fire and electrical-safety liability is not priced into the model. One incident is far worse than a bad towel.
GB/T variants, 1-phase vs 3-phase and CC/CP signalling cause compatibility returns, which take a lot of time for a part-timer.
With unsold stock written off, the stress test is -EUR 388, so the result depends on air-freighted stock actually selling.
Car lots that buy wholesale can import directly next time (0% duty, MOQ 1-2).
must_check_before_buying: Order paid samples from 2-3 suppliers. Have a licensed electrician test them on real BYD and VW-ID-China cars, and get CE DoC plus IEC 62196/62752 test reports in the supplier's name.
Pre-sell to 2-3 EV import lots with deposits before ordering 25 units.
Get a product-liability insurance quote.
Write a compatibility checklist (port type, phases, model year) and a returns policy before selling.
Confirm the China-Tirana air rate and the broker's classification (8536.69 / 8504.40).

ranking.niche: Premium car care and detailing products (own-brand home-wash kits, 5 L canisters for detailers)
ranking.verdict: Reject. The premium brands already have official Albanian distributors (GRT for Koch-Chemie and Ceramic Pro, Top Auto Parts for Sonax). Lavazh owners buy 20 kg shampoo for about EUR 50. Each SKU needs a CLP label and safety data sheet in Albanian, and the best-margin products are ADR dangerous goods. The kit makes about 10% if everything sells and loses about EUR 1,000 in the stress test.
key_reasons: Chemicals law 27/2016 and CLP DCM 488/2016 put labelling and SDS duties on the importer, which is paperwork a beginner underestimates.
Aerosols, sealants and wheel cleaners are dangerous goods for freight and couriers.
Single bottles sold on COD lose 22-83% because courier and ad costs exceed the basket.
B2B buyers are price-driven or already tied to GRT.
Seasonal (summer), so it needs an off-season plan.
must_check_before_buying: Only reconsider if a detailing studio signs a recurring written order. Otherwise do not proceed.

ranking.verdict: Reject as a business. Neptun, Megatek, Shpresa and Gjirafa50 sell 16 L units for EUR 145-200 with 24-month instalments, which is at or below what a small importer can land and deliver. Units are 13 kg, there is a 2-year compressor liability and the season is short. As a host-kit winter add-on it is fine, but buy locally against paid orders rather than importing.
key_reasons: Contribution is negative per unit in B2C even at a EUR 100 buy price.
The best all-B2B case is still -EUR 175 to -250 in the stress test.
Short season (Oct-Mar), and bulky stock that sits unsold for 9 months.
Grey-imported units have no local service network, so one failed compressor removes the margin on 5-10 units.
must_check_before_buying: Only as a pass-through add-on. Price it from Neptun or Megatek sale prices (Beko BDP010 at 12,999 ALL) with a service fee, taken from property managers with prepayment.

ranking.niche: Home backup power (LiFePO4 power stations and folding solar panels)
ranking.verdict: Reject. Each unit costs EUR 420-590 landed, so the budget buys only 4-6 units. The products are Class 9 dangerous goods for freight, couriers and warranty returns, duty is 10% unless a ruling says otherwise, and brand dealer access is unconfirmed. Brands discount heavily in the EU and Gjirafa50 and Foleja already stock EcoFlow and Anker. Under stress it loses EUR 270-895, and one warranty failure would wipe out the order.
key_reasons: Most outages are short (minutes), and cheap substitutes exist (router UPS, Temu power banks, generators).
Dangerous-goods logistics and returns are the worst kind of complexity for a beginner.
Few high-value units mean one COD refusal or one defect is a large share of capital.
The '40 outages a year, worst in Europe' figure is unverified. OSHEE says outages are falling, and I found no official SAIFI figure.
must_check_before_buying: Do not pursue it now. Revisit only with a confirmed dealer account, a binding ruling for HS 8504.40 at 0%, and pre-paid B2B orders.

challenged_claims.claim: Each dossier's single stress-test figure can be compared with the host-kit +EUR 100.
challenged_claims.problem: The dossiers treat unsold stock differently. Dehumidifier and EV (+112) and kitchen kits (+190) keep it as inventory. Power stations (-895) and water filters (+409) write it off. The car-care '-1,010' says 'counted at landed cost' but behaves like a write-off. Ranking on the headline numbers mixes these conventions.
challenged_claims.corrected_view: Approximate results on one basis. With stock written off: water about +409, EV -388, kitchen -416, power -895, car care about -1,010, dehumidifier well below -570. With stock kept: water about +990, kitchen +190, EV +112, power -273, dehumidifier -570. Restate the host-kit +EUR 100 on the same convention before any panel ranking.

challenged_claims.claim: The stress test is +EUR 409, so the numbers work on paper.
challenged_claims.problem: About 21 of the 30 cartridge sets are assumed to sell in 6 months, partly to 'existing RO owners of other brands'. Ecosoft's confirmed 1,390 ALL/month plan already includes filter changes, and the beginner's own RO buyers will not need cartridges within 6 months. Ad cost of EUR 20 and 12% no-shows are also optimistic for a high-consideration installed product from an unknown brand.
challenged_claims.corrected_view: Without third-party cartridge sales and at the dossier's pessimistic costs, the 6-month stress test is around -EUR 200 to -300. This is a pre-sold B2B add-on for rental flats and cafes, not a stock-first business.

challenged_claims.claim: No licence is needed to sell and install household filters.
challenged_claims.problem: This rests on finding no evidence of a licence. Installation is a service activity that touches building plumbing, with leak liability.
challenged_claims.corrected_view: Treat it as unverified until the QKB activity registration and any plumbing qualification rules are confirmed, and insurance is priced.

challenged_claims.claim: 50% of the 30 kits go B2B to hosts and property managers.
challenged_claims.problem: These are the same small group of buyers the host-kit plan already relies on. Counting their demand in both plans double-counts it. Buy prices are also estimates, and Korkmaz may route a small buyer to Arteg.
challenged_claims.corrected_view: Treat kitchen kits as a line on the host-kit order form (one customer, one pallet, one delivery), sized on deposits actually taken.

challenged_claims.claim: It roughly matches the benchmark on the stress test (+EUR 112 vs +EUR 100).
challenged_claims.problem: The figure keeps unsold stock and leaves out the cost of fire and electrical-safety liability and compatibility returns. The goods would come from Alibaba suppliers not yet vetted, by air.
challenged_claims.corrected_view: On money alone it is close (and -EUR 388 if stock is written off). After safety and support burden it ranks clearly below host kits for a beginner.

challenged_claims.claim: Albania has about 40 outages a year, the worst in Europe, so demand for backup power is strong.
challenged_claims.problem: The dossier found no official 2024-2025 SAIDI/SAIFI figure, and my search found none either. OSHEE claimed in Dec 2025 that outages are falling. The examples cited (Jan 2026 Tirana, June 2024 regional) lasted minutes to about 30 minutes, which a router UPS or power bank covers.
challenged_claims.corrected_view: The need for multi-hour backup is unproven. Do not size any stock on blackout news spikes.

challenged_claims.claim: Its most useful part is an auto-restart dehumidifier plus hygrometer imported as a host-kit add-on.
challenged_claims.problem: Even all-B2B, the import loses money. Importing 13 kg units for a few winter add-on orders adds freight and warranty exposure for nothing.
challenged_claims.corrected_view: Offer it as a pass-through: buy from Neptun or Megatek on sale against a prepaid order and add a small service fee. Do not import.

reviews.combo_idea: Kitchen kits combine best with host kits. They go to the same buyers (property managers and hosts in Tirana/Durres), on the same Turkish groupage pallet, with the same EUR.1 for 0% duty, and Denizli towel mills such as Hursan overlap with the host-kit textile supplier. Sell a 'rental flat starter pack' (bed sets, towels, lockbox, cookware set, 12 glasses) as one B2B order with a deposit. One broker fee and one freight charge then cover more value, which improves the host-kit margin. Off-season (Oct-Mar) fill: a winter damp-care add-on for empty rental flats (auto-restart dehumidifier plus hygrometer) bought locally on prepaid orders rather than imported. Later, an RO tap or filter-jug add-on for rental flats once the core business runs. Power stations, car care and EV gear go to different buyers or bring safety and dangerous-goods risk, so they do not combine well.
reviews.advice_to_beginner: None of the six new niches beats host kits as a business of its own, so keep host kits as the plan. Use this research to make that plan bigger, not to replace it. The most useful find is the kitchen kit as a second line on the same Turkish pallet for the same people. Before ordering anything, ask the hosts and property managers you already know whether they want bedding plus kitchen in one 'rental flat starter pack', and take deposits. Order only what is pre-paid plus a small buffer, with an EUR.1 and 'Made in Turkey' confirmed on every item. Leave out anything that needs installing, carries a lithium battery, is a chemical that needs its own label, or plugs into a car. In those lines one mistake (a leak, a fire, a dangerous-goods refusal, a 2-year warranty claim) costs more than your whole first year's profit. If you want a winter product, resell a locally bought dehumidifier to your rental clients on prepayment rather than importing one. Count your hours each month. Revisit water filters or EV adapters only after the host-kit business has paid back its first pallet and you have a few repeat B2B customers asking for them.

reviews.advisor: Albanian consumer and social-commerce marketer (scored host kits 52)

ranking.niche: Electric-car charging gear (Type 2 to GB/T adapters, portable mode-2 chargers; wallboxes only made to order)
ranking.verdict: This is the best stand-alone niche of the six, but it should be a narrow side line selling Type 2 to GB/T adapters and portable chargers, not a replacement for host kits. The buyer pain is sharp and easy to target, and there is more demand than the dossier claims. The market is small, buyers rarely come back, and car dealers could include the product with the car and close the gap overnight.
key_reasons: My spot check found demand the dossier understates. A Romanian report based on official data (gadget.ro) says about half of new cars sold in Albania in Jan-May 2026 were BYDs, roughly 4,000 units, and that all of them are the Chinese-market version. Bestsellingcarsblog puts BYD at about 40% of the 8,547 new cars sold in 2025. China-spec cars have GB/T inlets, so most new BYD owners need an adapter to use Type 2 public or OSHEE chargers.

The buyers are easy to reach and the product is easy to show. BYD and EV owner Facebook groups and MerrJep are the natural channels, and a 15-second video of an adapter turning a 'cannot charge' into 'charging' sells itself. Car lots selling grey-import Chinese EVs are an obvious B2B channel, which suits a part-timer with a day job.

It is a fit-it-or-not purchase, so COD refusals should run below the usual B2C rate once the buyer has confirmed by phone that the adapter fits their car. A typical order is EUR 110, well above the EUR 22 Temu duty-free limit, so Temu and AliExpress lose their price edge.
It sells all year with no seasonal peak, which offsets the summer peak of host kits.

The weak points: each owner buys once, so there are no repeat sales. AnGroup already sells the adapter at ALL 13,300 and Konekta sells portable chargers. If one car lot starts bundling the adapter with the car, a whole buyer group disappears. One overheating incident would destroy trust in a small word-of-mouth market.
must_check_before_buying: Ask 3-5 BYD sellers and car lots in Tirana whether new China-spec BYDs already come with a Type 2 to GB/T adapter or a GB/T portable charger. If they do, B2C demand collapses.
Check whether OSHEE public AC chargers have tethered cables or Type 2 sockets. That decides which adapter direction and current rating sell.
Order paid samples from 2 suppliers and test them on a real BYD Seagull, Song Plus or Sealion with a partner electrician. Get IEC 62196 test reports and CE documents.
Before ordering, pre-sell at least 10 adapters through owner groups and 1-2 car lots with deposits.
Get product-liability insurance quotes and put Albanian-language safety labels on every unit.

ranking.niche: Turkish-made home goods sold as 'new apartment' kitchen starter kits (cookware + Pasabahce glassware)
ranking.verdict: This does not work as its own business. On Instagram B2C it is a generic, crowded category, and the kit price is above what a buyer can put together locally. It is a very good add-on to host kits: the same buyers, the same Turkish groupage pallet, and the same broker fee.
key_reasons: Turkish brands carry no search interest: 'korkmaz' scores 0 in Google Trends Albania. Shoppers buy cookware on price and looks, not on the Turkish label.

B2C pricing does not hold up. A buyer can build the 'basic kit' locally for about ALL 7,800 (Novahome granite 4+1 set at ALL 4,990 plus two Arteg Pasabahce 6-glass sets at ALL 1,399), against the planned ALL 10,990. Large Instagram home-goods pages (about 133k followers) already sell granite sets with COD.

For B2B the kit solves the same 'furnish the rental flat in one order' problem as host kits. A property manager who buys linen and lockboxes will add a kitchen pack on the same invoice, and one delivery serves both.
Glass breaks in transit and in courier delivery, which leads to unhappy customers and refused COD parcels. This category produces bad reviews quickly.
Repeat purchase is low: one kit per flat, with occasional glass replacement.
must_check_before_buying: Get real wholesale quotes from Polat Cam and Marmara Zuccaciye. Korkmaz retail in Turkey is TL 7,999 (about EUR 144) for the Pera 8-piece and TL 3,849 (about EUR 69) for the Tombik Jr 6-piece, so EUR 60 for an 8-piece mid-line set looks optimistic.
Check that every SKU is marked 'Made in Turkey' and that the supplier issues EUR.1 or an origin declaration. Without them, duty is 15% on steel and 10% on glass.
Ask Arteg/Blunavi for a trade price as a local backup. If their trade price is close to the import cost, buy locally and skip the import paperwork.
Pre-sell the kitchen pack to the same 5-10 host-kit customers before adding it to the pallet. Do not stock for B2C.
Get food-contact declarations, and test double-boxing of glass with the courier.

ranking.niche: Water filtration with installation (under-sink RO, whole-house sediment filters, cartridge plan) in Tirana/Durres
ranking.verdict: The consumer pain is the strongest of the six, but this is a service business against trusted incumbents, and it clashes with a day job. Sell cartridges and point-of-use filters to hosts and cafes as an add-on rather than building an installation business.
key_reasons: The need is real and people already pay for it: bottled water at about ALL 36,400 a year, news on water rationing in Tirana, and doubts about whether tap water is safe to drink. It is a good story for videos, such as a before/after TDS meter test.

Few people search for it (Google Trends near 0), so leads come from word of mouth or paid ads. The buyer has to let a stranger drill under their sink, and trust in an unknown brand is the main barrier. Ecosoft/Teoren, Albafilters, Albuji and Aquafilter already offer free installation, water tests and long warranties.

The price ceiling is lower than the plan assumes. TeorenShop lists an Ecosoft 6-stage RO with mineralizer, 75 GPD membrane and a spare filter set at ALL 13,900 (about EUR 155). The planned ALL 24,000 installed price is hard to defend unless the installation is clearly worth the difference.
Cartridge refills give the repeat revenue host kits lack, but only after 6-12 months, and they need a reminder system.
Installation appointments in the evening or at weekends, plus liability for leaks into the flat below, are a heavy load for a part-timer.
must_check_before_buying: Call Teoren/Ecosoft Albania and Albafilters as a mystery shopper. Find out exactly what ALL 13,900 and ALL 1,390 a month include (installation, filter changes, who owns the unit).
Ask 10 hosts and 5 cafes whether they would pay for an RO tap or filtered-water jug service, and at what price.
Get leak-liability insurance quotes and agree a plumber's fee and backup plumber before quoting any price.
Test a sample RO unit for low water pressure on a roof-tank flat.

ranking.niche: Premium car care and detailing products (snow foam, sealants, microfibre, foam lances, 5 L canisters)
ranking.verdict: No. The premium end already has official distributors, car washes buy on price, and the DIY home-wash habit this plan relies on hardly exists in Tirana flats.
key_reasons: Most Albanian drivers live in apartments with no driveway, outdoor tap or space for a pressure washer, and in parts of Tirana water runs about 5 hours a day. A full wash at a lavazh costs EUR 6-10, so a EUR 79 home-wash kit with a foam lance has a very small B2C audience.

Enthusiasts are already served by GRT (official Koch-Chemie distributor), Top Auto Parts (Sonax), ADBL and K2 on GjirafaMall, and Instagram resellers such as @albaniadetailingofficial. A newcomer has no better price and no unique brand.
Detailing videos do well on TikTok, but the people watching them mostly buy from the shops already filming them.
Single items lose money once COD costs are paid, and many chemicals can't be shipped cheaply under ADR rules.
must_check_before_buying: Only reconsider this if 3+ detailing studios commit to an exclusive EU or Turkish brand that is not already sold in Albania.
Check CLP/SDS labelling cost and ADR status for each SKU before any quote.

ranking.niche: Home backup power: portable LiFePO4 power stations and folding solar panels
ranking.verdict: No. Each unit is expensive against an average wage of about EUR 1,000, most outages are short, cheap substitutes exist, and Gjirafa50 already sells the brands at prices close to EU levels.
key_reasons: A EUR 600-900 power station costs more than half to most of a month's gross wage. Buyers take time to decide and compare prices on Gjirafa50, Trendyol or with relatives abroad. COD refusals on high-priced parcels lock up cash.
Most outages last minutes, so a router UPS, a power bank from Temu or a fuel generator ('gjenerator ne shitje' is the top search) covers the need for far less money.
The strongest pitch is keeping the water pump running for hosts, but a pump plus a stand-alone UPS is cheaper and the local plumber or electrician already sells it.
The price gap is small: Gjirafa50 sells the EcoFlow River 2 Max at ALL 54,890 (about EUR 611), and Trendyol lists it at about EUR 560.
must_check_before_buying: Do not buy stock. Only consider made-to-order B2B with a 50% deposit after a dealer account and an HS 8504.40 (0% duty) ruling are confirmed.

ranking.niche: Compressor dehumidifiers and home-humidity products for damp coastal and new-build flats
ranking.verdict: No as a business: Neptun, Megatek and Shpresa sell at or below EU retail with 24-month instalments, and the B2C model loses money. Keep only hygrometers and moisture absorbers as a low-cost winter add-on for hosts.
key_reasons: A buyer in a damp flat walks into Neptun and gets a branded Beko or Ariston with warranty and instalments for ALL 13,000-17,000. An unknown Instagram seller at the same price with COD has nothing extra to offer.
The units weigh about 13 kg, so courier costs and refusals hurt, and the season runs October to March only.
Mould and condensation are popular topics on Telegrafi, so a winter 'damp check' content series would draw interest. A cheap hygrometer plus absorber bundle can earn a little from that.
A failed compressor under the 2-year seller liability, with no service network, can wipe out the profit on the whole order.
must_check_before_buying: Only as a host-kit add-on: ask property managers whether they would pay for a winter damp pack (hygrometer + absorbers, dehumidifier only on paid order with auto-restart). Confirm the HS 8479.89 classification if any dehumidifier is ever imported.

challenged_claims.claim: The share of GB/T-port cars is only inferred and not measured; EVs are 13.5% of first registrations, so the market is small.
challenged_claims.problem: The dossier undercounts China-spec cars. Trade press based on official data says about half of new cars sold in Jan-May 2026 were BYDs, roughly 4,000 units, all of them the Chinese-market version. Bestsellingcarsblog puts BYD at about 40% of 2025 new-car sales. The 13.5% figure mixes used imports into the total, and zero-km EV share was about 40% in 9M 2025 (57% BEV in Oct 2025).
challenged_claims.corrected_view: GB/T demand from new owners is much larger than the dossier assumes, which favours adapters. The real risk is that dealers already supply an adapter or a GB/T portable charger with the car, and that must be checked before buying.

challenged_claims.claim: Ecosoft/Teoren rents an installed RO system with filter changes for 13,900 ALL/yr prepaid.
challenged_claims.problem: The TeorenShop page I fetched is a product listing: the RO module, tank, tap, a spare filter set and a Filmtec membrane for 13,900 ALL. It does not mention installation, service or a rental contract, and it shows both 'sold out' and 'in stock'.
challenged_claims.corrected_view: Either way, a well-known brand sells RO hardware for about EUR 155. That caps the price harder than the model allows, and the planned 24,000 ALL installed price needs a strong installation and service story.

challenged_claims.claim: A basic kit at 10,990 ALL and a premium kit at 17,900 ALL can sell 50% B2C via Instagram/Facebook COD.
challenged_claims.problem: A buyer can assemble the basic kit from local shops for about 7,800 ALL (a Novahome granite 4+1 set at 4,990 plus two Arteg Pasabahce 6-glass sets at 1,399). Turkish brand names have no search interest, and big Instagram home pages already sell these products with COD.
challenged_claims.corrected_view: Treat it as a B2B convenience pack for hosts and property managers, priced into the host-kit order. Drop or minimise the B2C share.

challenged_claims.claim: A Korkmaz mid-line 8-piece stainless set can be bought for about EUR 60.
challenged_claims.problem: Korkmaz sets retail in Turkey at TL 7,999 for the Pera 8-piece (about EUR 144) and TL 3,849 for the Tombik Jr 6-piece (about EUR 69) at MediaMarkt TR. A wholesale price of EUR 60 for an 8-piece seems only possible on the cheapest lines.
challenged_claims.corrected_view: Budget EUR 75-95 for the premium set, or use cheaper unbranded Turkish stainless. The pessimistic case (stress test about -EUR 90) is more likely than the base case.

challenged_claims.claim: A EUR 79 home-wash starter kit with a foam lance can sell B2C on Instagram/TikTok.
challenged_claims.problem: The plan ignores how Albanians actually wash cars. Most urban owners live in apartments with no hose, driveway or pressure washer, Tirana has water only a few hours a day in places, and a lavazh wash costs EUR 6-10.
challenged_claims.corrected_view: The DIY audience is a small enthusiast group already served by GRT, Sonax and Instagram resellers, so B2C demand is overstated.

challenged_claims.claim: Gjirafa50 absorbers marked 'E shitur' show steady low-ticket demand.
challenged_claims.problem: 'E shitur' can simply mean sold out or out of stock on a listing. It shows neither volume nor how often items sell.
challenged_claims.corrected_view: Treat it as weak evidence. The real demand signal is the big chains stocking 10+ models each season, which is also the reason a newcomer cannot compete.

challenged_claims.claim: Albanians cannot buy cheaply from the brand because the EcoFlow EU store does not ship to Albania.
challenged_claims.problem: Albanian buyers have other routes: Trendyol (River 2 Max about EUR 560), relatives in Italy and Greece, and Gjirafa50 at about EUR 611. The local price gap is around 10%, not a protected margin.
challenged_claims.corrected_view: There is no real pricing gap for a small dealer, and price-checking by buyers will squeeze any markup.

reviews.combo_idea: The best fit is a Turkish 'rental-flat kitchen pack' (granite or stainless set, Pasabahce glasses, matching Turkish towels and bath mats). Add it to the same Turkish groupage pallet as the host-kit linen. It goes to the same property managers on the same invoice and shares the broker, scanning fee and EUR.1 paperwork. It raises the average B2B order and is pre-sold, not stocked for Instagram. For the winter off-season, offer a 'damp pack' for empty rental flats (hygrometer plus moisture absorbers, with an auto-restart dehumidifier only on paid order) and an RO tap or filtered-water jug option for hosts and cafes. EV adapters do not share buyers with host kits, but they sell all year and could be a second B2B side line through car lots once host kits are running.
reviews.advice_to_beginner: None of the six new niches beats host kits, so keep host kits as the main business. The cheapest way to grow is to sell more to the same property managers. Add a pre-sold Turkish kitchen pack to the same Turkish pallet, and offer a small winter damp pack so you have something to sell in the off-season. Don't start Instagram B2C for cookware, dehumidifiers, power stations or car care: chains, Gjirafa50 and Temu already win on price, trust and instalments. If you want a second line, EV adapters are the only one with a sharp, easy-to-reach pain, because new BYDs in Albania are China-spec with GB/T sockets. Before spending a euro, ask five BYD sellers whether they already include the adapter. Then test two samples on a real car and collect at least 10 deposits through EV owner groups and one or two car lots. Only then order about 15 units.

reviews.advisor: Skeptical CFO / unit-economics auditor (scored host kits 52, stress test about +EUR 100)

ranking.niche: Water filtration with installation (under-sink RO, whole-house sediment filters, cartridge plan) in Tirana/Durres
ranking.verdict: Best unit economics of the six on paper, but only as a made-to-order, deposit-backed service. Not yet proven to beat host kits once the cartridge timing, ad cost and incumbent pricing are fixed.
key_reasons: I reproduced the dossier: cash EUR 2,294, +EUR 2,055 if all sold, stress +EUR 409. Duty is 0% on 842121 and 842199 (WITS 2022, re-queried).

The stress test is on a stock-written-off basis. Counting unsold stock at cost, as the EV and kitchen dossiers do, it is +EUR 959. On the same basis my pessimistic case (RO 22,000 ALL, plumber EUR 40, ads EUR 45 per RO, sets EUR 10 ad) is still +EUR 337 at 70% of every line.

Most of the upside rests on 30 cartridge sets sold within 6 months. Your own RO buyers need no replacement until month 6-12. With realistic volumes (8 RO, 10 sets, 5 whole-house, 4 two-packs) the result falls to about EUR 0 with stock at cost, or about -EUR 890 if unsold stock is written off.

The price anchor is hostile. Teoren installs a 6-stage RO with a year of filters for 13,900 ALL, while the plan charges 24,000 ALL up front, 73% more in year 1. Ecosoft offers a 30-day free trial. Leads will cost more than EUR 20 per installed sale when Google Trends is near 0.
Hidden costs: about 40 h of plumbing visits, leak liability in apartments, 2-year seller liability on installed kit, and dependence on one plumber.
must_check_before_buying: Get written quotes from Aquafilter Europe, Aquamab or AFG for 12 RO units, cartridge sets and Big Blue housings, and check whether Aquafilter routes you to Aquafilter Albania.
Get a plumber's fixed per-install price in writing, plus a backup plumber, and a quote for liability insurance.
Pre-sell at least 6 installs on deposit (for example to rental hosts, cafes and offices you know) before ordering. If you cannot beat or match Teoren's 13,900 ALL year-1 offer, stop.
Confirm the actual terms of the Teoren and Ecosoft subscriptions (who owns the hardware, minimum term).
Check that the 'set fits other brands' claim holds for Ecosoft and Aquafilter housings, because the 30-set volume depends on it.
Ask a broker to confirm 0% on 8421.21 and 8421.99 for 2026, and get NSF/WRAS-type test reports.

ranking.niche: Turkish-made home goods sold as 'new apartment' kitchen starter kits (cookware + Pasabahce glassware)
ranking.verdict: Loses as a standalone business but is the best add-on: same buyers (hosts, property managers) and same Turkey groupage and paperwork as the host kits.
key_reasons: I reproduced it: kit landed cost EUR 55.7 (basic) and EUR 90.8 (premium), +EUR 907 contribution if all sold, stress +EUR 185 with stock at cost, -EUR 422 if unsold stock is written off.

The margin is fragile. With buy prices 20% higher and EUR 16 ads per B2C sale, the stress test is -EUR 83 (-EUR 118 if only 30% sells B2B). Without valid EUR.1 (15% on 732393 and 10% on 701337, both confirmed on WITS) it is +EUR 44.

The Korkmaz buy price of EUR 60 is optimistic for mid-line sets. Turkish retail is about 6,400 TL for Tombik 8-pc (Koctas/Teknosa) and 4,499-6,100 TL for Perla. Only Perla-class lines fit EUR 60; expect EUR 70-80 through a wholesaler such as Polat Cam.
Single items lose money (a Pasabahce set sold alone is -82%), so the plan only works as bundled kits, mostly B2B.
Korkmaz and Pasabahce are already distributed by Arteg/Blunavi; the only edge is the bundle and convenience. Glass breakage stays with the buyer.
must_check_before_buying: Get a Polat Cam or Marmara Zuccaciye quote per SKU, and a 'Made in Turkey' confirmation plus EUR.1 for every SKU.
Check whether the 8-pc set at EUR 60 is Perla-class rather than Tombik.
Get supplier food-contact declarations of compliance for coated aluminium and glass.
Pre-sell at least 10 kits to the host-kit customers before ordering.
Ship only on the same pallet as the host kits.

ranking.niche: Electric-car charging gear (Type 2 to GB/T adapters, portable mode-2 chargers; wallboxes made to order)
ranking.verdict: Roughly matches host kits only under base assumptions and turns clearly negative with realistic freight and ad costs. The safety liability is far higher than for towels.
key_reasons: I reproduced it: adapter landed EUR 38.4, charger EUR 109.1, +EUR 353 if all sold, stress +EUR 112 with stock at cost (-EUR 388 if written off). Duty is 0% on 853669, 850440 and 854442 (WITS confirmed).

Pessimistic case (air express EUR 10/kg rather than 7, buy prices +20%, adapter cut to 8,900 ALL to compete, EUR 25 ads per B2C sale): adapter contribution EUR 12.6, portable charger -EUR 4.7, stress -EUR 351 (about -EUR 960 if written off).
All buy prices come from unquoted Alibaba listings. The adapter price ceiling is set by AliExpress (about EUR 50-85 delivered with VAT) and AnGroup's 13,300 ALL.
Zero duty means any car lot or electrician can import the same goods directly, so B2B buyers can become competitors.
There is fire and compatibility liability (CC/CP signalling, 1- versus 3-phase) and a support load for someone with a day job. The GB/T share of the fleet is not measured.
must_check_before_buying: Get a firm DDP or air-express quote China to Tirana for 35 kg.
Order paid samples and get the IEC 62196 and IEC 62752 test reports.
Get pre-orders from 2-3 Chinese-EV import car lots.
Count how many GB/T-port cars those lots actually sell each month.
Get product-liability insurance cost.

ranking.niche: Premium car care and detailing products (own-brand home-wash kits + 5 L B2B canisters)
ranking.verdict: Loses. The stress number in the dossier is overstated, but the corrected figure is still negative, and the official distributors (GRT/Koch, Top Auto Parts/Sonax) already serve the B2B buyers.
key_reasons: The dossier's -EUR 1,010 stress figure writes off unsold stock, even though its notes say stock is 'counted at landed cost'. Recomputed with stock at cost, it is about -EUR 296 (including the EUR 100 launch cost). That is still clearly negative.
Kit contribution is only EUR 6.71 (10%). Any slip in courier, ads or refusals wipes it out, and single items lose 22-83%.
Heavy, low-value liquids, Albanian CLP labels and SDS, and ADR rules on the most profitable SKUs (sealants, wheel cleaners, aerosols).
Lavazh B2B buyers pay about EUR 50 for 20 kg of bulk shampoo, so premium canisters have no volume.
must_check_before_buying: Do not proceed. If it is revisited, get Setkim or Interwax private-label MOQs and EUR.1, and an SDS translation quote.

ranking.verdict: Loses. Albanian chains sell at or below EU retail with instalment plans, so a small importer has negative contribution even with 0% duty.
key_reasons: Duty is 0% under 847989 (WITS confirmed); under 841582 it would be 10% (also confirmed). The classification risk is real but does not matter, because the numbers are negative anyway.
Neptun sells a Beko 10 L for 12,999 ALL (EUR 120.6 net of VAT). BigBuy's cheapest 12 L is about EUR 102 before freight, courier and warranty.
Dossier: -EUR 168 if all sold, stress -EUR 570 (contribution on sold units, stock kept at cost; about -EUR 1,300 if written off). I agree with the direction.
The only workable part is a made-to-order auto-restart unit plus hygrometer for property managers' empty winter flats, bought against a paid order.
must_check_before_buying: Do not stock. If a property manager pre-pays, source one unit from BigBuy or a local wholesaler per order.

ranking.niche: Home backup power: portable LiFePO4 power stations and folding solar panels
ranking.verdict: Loses badly. Few high-value units carry dangerous-goods freight, 10% duty and warranty risk, and EU street prices cap the Albanian price.
key_reasons: Duty on 850760 is 10% (WITS confirmed). The 0% alternative under 8504.40 is unlikely: UK advance rulings classify lithium power banks under 8507.60, and the battery gives the unit its essential character. Plan on 10%.
Dossier stress test: -EUR 890 written off, -EUR 273 with stock at cost. Contribution is only about 13% on a EUR 890 sale, and the panel is negative.
Over 100 Wh these are Class 9 dangerous goods. Warranty returns mean shipping DG back to the EU, with no service centre in Albania.
Gjirafa50 and Foleja already stock EcoFlow and Anker SOLIX; outages are mostly short; substitutes (UPS units, generators, Temu power banks) are cheap.
must_check_before_buying: Do not proceed. At most, act as a referral or agent for a pre-paid B2B order once a dealer account and the DG freight cost are confirmed.

challenged_claims.claim: Stress-test figures are comparable with each other and with the host-kit +EUR 100
challenged_claims.problem: The dossiers use different conventions. Water (+409) and car care (-1,010) write off unsold stock. EV (+112), kitchen (+190) and dehumidifier (-570) keep it at cost. Power reports both. The ranking therefore mixes bases.
challenged_claims.corrected_view: On a stock-at-cost basis: water +959 (pessimistic +337, realistic mix about 0), kitchen +185, EV +112, car care about -296, power -273, dehumidifier -570. Written off: water +409, EV -388, kitchen -422, power -890, car care -1,010, dehumidifier about -1,300. The host-kit +EUR 100 must be restated on the same basis before any niche is said to beat it.

challenged_claims.claim: Stress test -EUR 1,010 with 'unsold stock counted at landed cost'
challenged_claims.problem: The arithmetic only reproduces if all unsold stock is written off (sold revenue minus variable costs minus the landed cost of all 58 units minus 450 minus 100).
challenged_claims.corrected_view: With stock at cost it is about -EUR 296. That is still negative and still loses to host kits, but by less.

challenged_claims.claim: 30 annual cartridge sets sold within the 6-month window, and an ad cost of EUR 20 per installed RO sale
challenged_claims.problem: Your own RO buyers do not need replacements until month 6-12, and selling to owners of other brands needs a fitment check. Search volume is near 0, and incumbents offer free trials, so EUR 20 per high-consideration install is optimistic.
challenged_claims.corrected_view: With 8 RO, 10 sets, 5 whole-house filters, 4 two-packs, plumber EUR 40 and ads EUR 45 per RO, the result is about EUR 0 with stock at cost (about -EUR 890 if written off). The niche works only if installs are pre-sold.

challenged_claims.claim: The offer is competitive because over 3 years it costs less than Ecosoft's subscription (37,500 against 41,700 ALL)
challenged_claims.problem: Buyers compare year-1 cash. Teoren installs a 6-stage RO with a year of filters for 13,900 ALL; the plan asks 24,000 ALL.
challenged_claims.corrected_view: Expect to match a sub-15,000 ALL year-1 entry price or to sell mostly B2B (rentals, offices), which lowers the RO margin. Model RO at 18,000-20,000 ALL.

challenged_claims.claim: Korkmaz mid-line 8-pc stainless set buy price EUR 60
challenged_claims.problem: Turkish retail for Tombik 8-pc is about 6,400 TL (Koctas, Teknosa), roughly EUR 115 at 55.6 TL/EUR, or about EUR 96 ex-KDV. EUR 60 is distributor pricing, and Korkmaz already has an Albanian distributor (Arteg/Blunavi).
challenged_claims.corrected_view: Use EUR 70-80 through a wholesaler, or the Perla line (from 4,499 TL). With buy prices +20% and realistic ads, the stress test is -EUR 83.

challenged_claims.claim: Duty 0% on Turkish origin
challenged_claims.problem: This is true only with valid EUR.1 or an origin declaration and genuine Turkish manufacture. Without it the duty is 15% on stainless (732393) and 10% on glass (701337), both confirmed on WITS.
challenged_claims.corrected_view: Without EUR.1 the stress test falls from +185 to about +44. Make 'Made in Turkey' plus EUR.1 per SKU a condition of payment.

challenged_claims.claim: A power station could be classed under 8504.40 at 0% duty
challenged_claims.problem: National rulings (UK advance tariff rulings) put lithium power banks under 8507.60, the battery being the essential character, and no ruling for 8504.40 was found.
challenged_claims.corrected_view: Budget 10% duty. A binding ruling would most likely confirm 8507.60.

challenged_claims.claim: Air express from China at EUR 7/kg, and adapter and charger buy prices of EUR 30 and EUR 85
challenged_claims.problem: Both are unquoted estimates. A 35 kg air-express shipment from China usually costs more per kg, and Alibaba listing prices often exclude CE paperwork and packaging.
challenged_claims.corrected_view: At EUR 10/kg, buy prices +20% and an adapter price cut to 8,900 ALL, the stress test is -EUR 351. Get a DDP quote before deciding.

challenged_claims.claim: EVs are 44% of new-car registrations
challenged_claims.problem: Monitor data shows 13.5% of all first registrations (new plus used) in Jan-Apr 2026, and the share of cars with GB/T ports, which is what drives adapter demand, is not measured.
challenged_claims.corrected_view: Size demand on car-lot pre-orders, not on registration share.

reviews.combo_idea: Kitchen kits on the same Turkey groupage pallet as the host kits. They go to the same buyers (hosts and property managers furnishing flats), use the same Denizli/Istanbul sourcing route, and share one broker fee, one scanning fee and the EUR.1 paperwork. Sharing saves about EUR 160 of the kit's EUR 242 fixed cost and most of its EUR 300 freight, which improves the kit stress test by about EUR 300. Offer it as an optional kitchen pack in the host-kit offer, pre-sold on deposit. Second, a made-to-order service line for the same B2B accounts: an under-sink RO or jug filter for rental flats and cafes, plus an auto-restart dehumidifier with hygrometer for empty winter flats (Oct-Mar). It helps fill the host kits' off-season, but only against paid orders, never as stock.
reviews.advice_to_beginner: None of the six new niches clearly beats the host kits once the numbers are put on the same basis and stressed. Dehumidifiers, power stations and car care lose money even on the dossiers' own figures. EV charging gear only breaks even if every estimated buy price and freight rate turns out right, and the fire and compatibility risk is not worth it for a part-timer. Keep the host kits as the core business. Pre-sell them to people you know, and before ordering restate the +EUR 100 stress test with unsold stock counted at cost, so it compares fairly with these figures. Add Turkish kitchen packs only on the same pallet and only against deposits. Treat water filtration as a later experiment: first get one plumber's fixed price and 5-6 paid installs from your host and property-manager contacts, and price against Teoren's 13,900 ALL year-1 offer. If that works, cartridge refills can give you repeat income in winter. Do not spend money on any line until you have a written supplier quote, origin proof where duty depends on it, and paid demand.
